intelligence.essence: No bottom bar at all, and no top bar blocking — the big buttons and the massive bar take up all the space, block the view, and make the slides unreadable. The final shape: just a nice beautiful Keep Reading button and a little back button beside it, small at the bottom, looking like part of the presentation itself. Back and forward use the calendar's own day forward/back logic. No slide count anywhere. The headline sits at the top and folds away on scroll. No name at the door — the name is asked at the end, with the Collective Agreement. The label is just "NAYA". A new picture of her on every slide, switching sides; the red N in some spots, cropped from the title card that arrived 12:20 MST. And nothing reaches him until the captain has walked every viewpoint of every frame.
